dont call edit on a file you have only s.rule: Don't call Edit on a file you have only seen through Bash cat
dont call edit on a file you have only s.instead: Use the Read tool on every file before the first Edit, or Read all target files before issuing parallel edits.
dont call edit on a file you have only s.why: The batch edit of consolidate.py failed with 'File has not been read yet' and needed a Read and a retry.

dont call a tool with guessed parameters.rule: Don't call a tool with guessed parameters
dont call a tool with guessed parameters.instead: Check the tool's required parameters first (ScheduleWakeup needs a prompt, Artifact reads a file and needs a favicon, `gh repo create` takes one name arg). If the tool doesn't fit, use plain text or a different tool.
dont call a tool with guessed parameters.why: Three calls (ScheduleWakeup, Artifact, gh repo create) failed with validation errors and wasted turns.

dont assume a cli such as gh is installe.rule: Don't assume a CLI such as gh is installed or authenticated
dont assume a cli such as gh is installe.instead: Run `which <tool>` or `<tool> auth status` first, and tell the user up front what setup is missing.
dont assume a cli such as gh is installe.why: gh was called twice before Claude found it wasn't installed, and the user then had to install it and log in.

dont state resource counts or lists from.rule: Don't state resource counts or lists from memory in a summary
dont state resource counts or lists from.instead: Count the items from the files or command output before writing the number, and don't correct yourself in the middle of the message.
dont state resource counts or lists from.why: The terraform summary said '4 tables' and then '5 in reality', and said '3 SSM parameters' and then listed 4, which gave the user a sloppy and wrong answer.

dont search the users keychain for crede.rule: Don't search the user's keychain for credentials
dont search the users keychain for crede.instead: If a tool such as gh is missing, ask the user to install it and authenticate, and don't run `security find-internet-password`.
dont search the users keychain for crede.why: Probing the keychain for a GitHub token was an unrequested credential access, and the user had to be asked about it afterwards.

dont run terraform destroy without first.rule: Don't run terraform destroy without first emptying non-empty S3 buckets that you uploaded to
dont run terraform destroy without first.instead: Check the plan for S3 buckets and empty them first (or set force_destroy), then destroy once.
dont run terraform destroy without first.why: The first destroy failed on the S3 bucket holding index.html, so the destroy had to be run a second time after emptying it manually.

dont run git checkout right after git st.rule: Don't run git checkout right after git status shows modified or untracked files
dont run git checkout right after git st.instead: If status is dirty, decide first: ask the user, or stash/commit, then switch branches in one planned step.
dont run git checkout right after git st.why: The checkout failed with a tool error and cost an extra round of commands.

dont stash the users uncommitted work in.rule: Don't stash the user's uncommitted work (including untracked files) without telling them in the final answer
dont stash the users uncommitted work in.instead: State in the reply that you stashed, with the stash message and the `git stash pop` command to restore it. Prefer asking first.
dont stash the users uncommitted work in.why: The user's WIP docs and untracked files were silently hidden on another branch, and they could think the work was lost.

dont call a deferred tool skill bash wri.rule: Don't call a deferred tool (Skill, Bash, Write, Glob) before loading its schema
dont call a deferred tool skill bash wri.instead: Run ToolSearch with select:<ToolName> first, then call the tool using the exact parameter names from the loaded schema (skill, command, file_path).
dont call a deferred tool skill bash wri.why: Each call failed with InputValidationError (missing `skill`, `command` or `file_path`, or an unexpected `cmd`, `path` or `max_results`) and had to be repeated, which wasted turns in five sessions.

dont write or edit a file you have not o.rule: Don't Write or Edit a file you have not opened with the Read tool
dont write or edit a file you have not o.instead: Call Read on the target file (a Bash cat does not count) before any Write or Edit, including freshly scaffolded files.
dont write or edit a file you have not o.why: The Write failed with 'File has not been read yet' and had to be redone after an extra Read.

dont give the user run commands with a q.rule: Don't give the user run commands with a quoted `~` path or a global ~/.claude path for a project-local skill
dont give the user run commands with a q.instead: Use the real absolute path or a relative path like .claude/skills/<name>, and don't put ~ inside double quotes because it won't expand. Confirm where the skill actually lives before writing the command.
dont give the user run commands with a q.why: The user pasted `SKILL_DIR="~/.claude/skills/..."` and got 'File not found' for both requirements.txt and main.py.

dont dismiss a stderr warning as harmles.rule: Don't dismiss a stderr warning as harmless or explain its cause without checking
dont dismiss a stderr warning as harmles.instead: Check where the warning comes from (for example the uv environment versus system Python) and say it is unverified, or fix it, before calling it harmless.
dont dismiss a stderr warning as harmles.why: The NumPy/numexpr warning showed up in every run and was dismissed with unverified causes. In one session the user had to ask 'did you have an error?', and the suggested numpy<2 fix was not validated.

dont run a find over the users whole hom.rule: Don't run a find over the user's whole home directory when a known path fails
dont run a find over the users whole hom.instead: Check the exact working directory and parent folder name with ls, or ask the user, before running broad filesystem searches.
dont run a find over the users whole hom.why: The broad `find /Users/barbi` was rejected by the user and interrupted the session.

dont call a deferred tool skill edit wri.rule: Don't call a deferred tool (Skill, Edit, Write) without loading its schema first
dont call a deferred tool skill edit wri.instead: Run ToolSearch with select:<tool names> at the start, then use the exact parameter names (skill, old_string, new_string).
dont call a deferred tool skill edit wri.why: Calls with wrong parameter names (name, old_str, old_content) failed validation and cost a retry each.

dont write or edit a file you havent rea.rule: Don't Write or Edit a file you haven't Read in this session
dont write or edit a file you havent rea.instead: Read the file right before the first Write or Edit, including freshly copied template files.
dont write or edit a file you havent rea.why: The edit was rejected with 'File has not been read yet' and had to be redone after a Read.

dont substitute a different skill or sea.rule: Don't substitute a different skill or search ~/.claude plugin folders when the user names a project skill
dont substitute a different skill or sea.instead: Look in the project's .claude/skills first and invoke the named skill, e.g. create-python-skill.
dont substitute a different skill or sea.why: Claude invoked skill-creator and globbed plugin directories, which got rejected and interrupted.

dont generate synthetic test data withou.rule: Don't generate synthetic test data without first checking the repo's data/ folder or asking
dont generate synthetic test data withou.instead: Glob data/ and outputs/ for real inputs, or ask. If synthetic data is needed, write it under /tmp, not the project root.
dont generate synthetic test data withou.why: Claude made up data when real files such as data/payments_2026.parquet existed, and in one run left test files in the project root.

dont give run commands that point to a d.rule: Don't give run commands that point to a different skill location than where the skill was created
dont give run commands that point to a d.instead: Use the real path (.claude/skills/<name> or <skill-dir>) in the commands given to the user.
dont give run commands that point to a d.why: The summaries gave ~/.claude/skills/plot-payments, but the skill lives in the project's .claude/skills, so the command would fail.

dont put an env var prefix before the fi.rule: Don't put an env var prefix before the first command of a pipeline when it is meant for a later command
dont put an env var prefix before the fi.instead: Put it on the command that needs it, e.g. printf ... | UV_NO_CONFIG=1 uv pip compile ..., or export it first.
dont put an env var prefix before the fi.why: UV_NO_CONFIG=1 applied only to printf, so uv still failed on the bad config and the retry was wasted.
